key_insight: The nonlinear entropy-stable extension of Navier–Stokes–Fourier becomes a fourth-order quasi-cubic system in entropy variables, while its quasi-linear approximation retains entropy stability and the highest-order derivative terms.
engineering_relevance: The closure offers a promising route to improved rarefied-gas heat-transfer predictions beyond standard continuum equations.
method: Derive the entropy-variable formulation using an inverse collision-operator derivative identity.
Apply the quasi-linear approximation to stationary heat transfer between parallel plates.
Analyze plane-wave dispersion in the one-dimensional linearized equations.
evidence_signal: For parallel-plate heat transfer, selected boundary conditions yield temperature profiles closer to DSMC and heat flux closer to Sherman–Lees predictions than the stated Navier–Stokes–Fourier baselines; all frequency modes in the linearized dispersion study are stable.
watch_item: Reported heat-transfer improvements depend on boundary-condition specification, and the abstract does not establish performance in complex geometries or turbulent flows.
paper_title: Extensions to the Navier-Stokes-Fourier Equations for Rarefied Transport: Entropy Variable Formulation, Heat Transfer and Dispersion of a Non-Linear Entropy Stable Closure
